title.sourceEnglish: Understanding Your Soil: The Foundation of Everything
title.sesothoDraft: Ho Utlwisisa Mobu wa Hao: Motheo wa Ntho e Nngwe le e Nngwe

body.sourceEnglish:
Soil contains many kinds of living organisms. Bacteria and fungi help break down organic matter and cycle nutrients.

Some fungi help roots take up nutrients. Worm channels can help water and air enter soil.

Look at roots, soil structure and water movement as well as visible soil life.

Put soil and water in a clear jar, with a little suitable dispersing detergent. Close and shake it, then leave it undisturbed.

Sand settles first. Silt settles next, while clay can remain suspended much longer.

This is a rough learning exercise. Clumps and unsettled clay can mislead you; use a soil laboratory when accurate texture is needed.

A thick sand layer beneath cloudy water does not yet tell you the final proportions. Some fine particles may still be suspended.

Compare the settled layers and feel the soil in the field.

Record what you see and what remains uncertain. Do not prescribe watering or soil treatments from one jar alone.

Compaction, poor drainage and loss of organic matter can limit roots and soil life.

Pale colour or few worms do not prove that chemicals killed the soil. Worm activity also changes with moisture and season.

Look for patterns across the field. Check management history, drainage and plant growth before choosing a remedy.
body.sesothoDraft:
Mobung ho na le mefuta e mengata ya dintho tse phelang. Baktheria le fungi di thusa ho qhaqha organic matter le ho tsamaisa dimatlafatsi ka potoloho.

Fungi tse ding di thusa metso ho monya dimatlafatsi. Meselana e entsweng ke diboko e ka thusa metsi le moya ho kena mobung.

Sheba metso, sebopeho sa mobu le motsamao wa metsi, hammoho le dintho tse phelang mobung tse bonahalang.

Kenya mobu le metsi ka clear jar, o kenye hanyenyane ya suitable dispersing detergent. E kwale mme o e sisinye, ebe o e siya e sa sisinyehe.

Sand e dula fatshe pele. Silt e latela, athe clay e ka nna ya dula e suspended nako e telele haholo.

Ena ke rough learning exercise feela. Dikgobokano tsa mobu (clumps) le clay e so duleng fatshe di ka o kgelosa; sebedisa soil laboratory ha o hloka soil texture e nepahetseng.

Lera le letenya la sand ka tlasa cloudy water ha le eso o bolelle final proportions. Fine particles tse ding di ka nna tsa dula di suspended.

Bapisa likarolo tse lutseng, ’me u utloe mobu tšimong.

Ngola seo u se bonang le seo u sa kholisehang ka sona. U se ke ua etsa qeto ea ho nosetsa kapa ho alafa mobu ka lebaka la nkho e le ’ngoe feela.

Ho thatafala ha mobu (compaction), drainage e mpe le tahlehelo ya organic matter di ka sitisa metso le bophelo ba mobu.

Mmala o lerootho kapa palo e nyane ya diboko ha e pake hore dikhemikhale di bolaile mobu. Mosebetsi wa diboko le wona o a fetoha ho latela mongobo le sehla.

Batla mekhoa e iphetang tšimong. Hlahloba nalane ea tsamaiso, metsi a phallang le kholo ea limela pele u khetha tharollo.

title.sesothoDraft: Ho Etsa le ho Sebedisa Kompose (Compost)

body.sourceEnglish:
Compost is organic matter broken down under managed conditions.

Finished compost can improve soil structure and contribute nutrients.

Time to readiness varies with materials, moisture, air and temperature. A province name or a fixed number of weeks is not a readiness test.

Mix dry browns with fresh greens. Avoid thick, wet layers that keep air out.

If the heap becomes slimy or smells strongly of ammonia, add dry browns and turn it.

Check moisture and air as the heap changes; one recipe does not suit every mix of materials.

A hot centre does not prove that every part of a heap has been treated. Time, temperature and management all matter.

Keep meat, dairy, diseased plants, pet waste and contaminated materials out of this simple household system.

Do not assume home composting destroys every weed seed or disease organism. Use a recognised process where sanitation is required.

Keep wattle seed pods out of the compost heap. An ordinary heap may not make every seed non-viable.

Use only clean, untreated materials. Bark breaks down slowly; its name alone is not proof that it is free of contamination.

Check the heap and turn when it needs more air or mixing. Keep it moist rather than waterlogged.
body.sesothoDraft:
Compost ke organic matter e qhaqhollwang ka tsela e laolwang.

Compost e phethilweng e ka ntlafatsa sebopeho sa mobu mme ya fana ka dimatlafatsi.

Nako ya hore compost e lokele ho sebediswa e fapana ho ya ka materials, mongobo, moya le thempereitjha. Lebitso la province kapa palo e behilweng ya dibeke ha se readiness test.

Kopanya dry browns le fresh greens. Qoba layers tse teteaneng, tse metsi tse thibelang moya ho kena.

Ha qubu ya compost e ka ba slimy kapa e nkha ammonia haholo, eketsa dry browns mme o e phethole.

Hlahloba mongobo le moya ha qubu ya compost e ntse e fetoha; recipe e le nngwe ha e tshwanele motswako o mong le o mong wa materials.

Karolo e bohareng e tjhesang ya qubu ha e pake hore karolo e nngwe le e nngwe ya yona e se e treated. Nako, temperature le management kaofela di bohlokwa.

Boloka meat, dairy, diseased plants, pet waste le contaminated materials di le ka ntle ho tsamaiso ena e bonolo ya lapeng.

U se ke ua nahana hore home composting e fedisa peo e nngwe le e nngwe ya mofoka kapa disease organism e nngwe le e nngwe. Sebedisa recognised process moo sanitation e hlokahalang.

Boloka wattle seed pods di le ka ntle ho qubu ya compost. Qubu e tlwaelehileng e ka nna ya se etse hore peo e nngwe le e nngwe e be non-viable.

Sebedisa materials tse hlwekileng feela, tse sa alafwang. Bark e bola butle; lebitso la yona feela ha le pake hore ha e na contamination.

Hlahloba qubu ya compost mme o e phethole ha e hloka moya o mongata kapa ho kopanngwa. E boloke e le mongobo, e se ke ya ba waterlogged.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Balance browns, greens, moisture and air
keyPoints.sesothoDraft: Lekanyetsa tse sootho, tse tala, mongobo le moya

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: A hot centre does not prove the whole heap is sanitised
keyPoints.sesothoDraft: Karolo e bohareng e chesang ha e pake hore qubu yohle e sanitised.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Keep seed pods and contaminated materials out
keyPoints.sesothoDraft: Boloka makgapha a dipeo le disebediswa tse nang le ditshila kantle

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Judge readiness from the compost condition, not a fixed regional timetable
keyPoints.sesothoDraft: Ahlola ho loka ho tswa boemong ba kompose, eseng lenaneong le behilweng la nako la lebatowa

question.sourceEnglish: A farmer's compost heap smells strongly of ammonia and is wet and slimy. What's the fix?
question.sesothoDraft: Qubu ya compost ya molemi e nkha ammonia haholo mme e metsi ebile e slimy. Tharollo ke efe?

options.sourceEnglish: Add more nitrogen-rich green material
options.sesothoDraft: Eketsa disebediswa tse tala tse nang le naetrojene e ngata

options.sourceEnglish: Add more dry carbon material like straw and turn the heap
options.sesothoDraft: Eketsa disebediswa tse omileng tsa khabone (carbon) jwalo ka jwang bo omileng (straw) mme o phethole qubu

options.sourceEnglish: Stop turning it and let it cool
options.sesothoDraft: Kgaotsa ho e phethola mme o e tlohele e fole

options.sourceEnglish: Add more water — the smell means it's too dry
options.sesothoDraft: Eketsa metsi a mangata — monko o bolela hore e omeletse haholo

rationale.sourceEnglish: A wet, slimy heap may need more air and drier material. Add dry browns and turn the heap to open it up. An ammonia smell can also suggest too much nitrogen-rich material. Check that the heap stays damp, not soggy.
rationale.sesothoDraft: Qubu e metsi, e slimy e ka hloka moya o mongata le material e ommeng ho feta. Eketsa dry browns mme o phethole qubu hore e bulehe mme moya o kene. Monko wa ammonia le wona o ka bontsha hore ho na le material e ngata haholo e nang le nitrogen. Hlahloba hore qubu e dule e le damp, e se be soggy.

question.sourceEnglish: Why keep wattle seed pods out of an ordinary compost heap?
question.sesothoDraft: Ke hobaneng ha o lokela ho boloka makgapha a dipeo tsa wattle kantle ho qubu e tlwaelehileng ya kompose?

options.sourceEnglish: Bark makes every heap too hot
options.sesothoDraft: Makgapetla a difate a etsa hore qubu e nngwe le e nngwe e tjhese haholo

options.sourceEnglish: Some seeds may survive and spread when the compost is used
options.sesothoDraft: Dipeo tse ding di ka nna tsa pholoha mme tsa nama ha kompose e sebediswa

options.sourceEnglish: Pods always attract termites
options.sesothoDraft: Makgapha a dula a hulela mohlwa kamehla

options.sourceEnglish: Pods release a gas that kills every soil organism
options.sesothoDraft: Makgapha a lokolla kgase e bolayang setshedi se seng le se seng sa mobu

rationale.sourceEnglish: An ordinary heap may not expose every seed to conditions that make it non-viable. Excluding pods avoids spreading them with the compost.
rationale.sesothoDraft: Qubu e tlwaelehileng e ka nna ya se pepesetse peo e nngwe le e nngwe maemong a ka e etsang hore e se hlole e kgona ho mela (non-viable). Ho ntsha makgapha a dipeo ho thibela hore a se ke a nama mmoho le kompose.

infographicAlt.sourceEnglish: Two patches of soil under the same sun: bare ground cracked and dry, mulched ground still dark and moist.
infographicAlt.sesothoDraft: Dikarolo tse pedi tsa soil ka tlasa letsatsi le le leng: mobu o sa kwahelwang o petsohile mme o omme; mobu o kwahetsweng ka mulch o ntse o le lefifi ebile o le mongobo.

title.sourceEnglish: Mulching and Cover Crops: Protecting and Building Soil
title.sesothoDraft: Ho Sebedisa Mulch le Dijalo tse Sireletsang Mobu (Cover Crops): Ho Sireletsa le ho Aha Mobu

body.sourceEnglish:
Cover bare soil with suitable clean mulch, such as straw, dry grass or wood chips.

Mulch can reduce evaporation, soften the impact of rain and suppress weeds.

Keep it clear of trunks and stems. Check moisture underneath and adjust the layer; more mulch is not always better.

Cover crops can protect ground between main crops. Choose for local weather, available water and the next planting.

The course examples include oats, lupins, sunn hemp and cowpea. Check local suitability before sowing.

Legumes need suitable bacteria and growing conditions to fix nitrogen. Nutrients in their residues become available as the material decomposes.

Worm farms can turn suitable food scraps and bedding into castings. Check the bin rather than expecting a fixed harvest date.

Liquid that drains naturally from a worm bin is called leachate. It is not the same as a prepared worm-casting tea.

Leachate can contain harmful organisms or substances. Do not use it on edible plants or assume that dilution makes it safe.

A Highveld field left bare after the maize harvest faces two main risks.

Winter wind can carry away dry topsoil.

The first heavy spring storm can strike bare ground and damage its surface and structure. If water runs over the field, it can carry loosened soil away.

Cover crops, mulch, and organic matter can help hold soil in place and help it stay alive.
body.sesothoDraft:
Koahela mobu o pepesitsweng ka mulch e hlwekileng e loketseng, jwalo ka straw, dry grass kapa wood chips.

Mulch e ka fokotsa evaporation, ya fokotsa matla ao pula e otlang mobu ka ona, mme ya fokotsa kgolo ya mefoka.

E boloke e le hole le trunks and stems. Hlahloba mongobo ka tlasa mulch mme o fetole layer ha ho hlokahala; mulch e ngata ha e dule e le betere.

Cover crops di ka sireletsa mobu pakeng tsa main crops. Di kgethe ho latela boemo ba lehodimo ba sebakeng sa heno, metsi a fumanehang le next planting.

Mehlala ya thuto ena e kenyelletsa oats, lupins, sunn hemp le cowpea. Hlahloba hore di loketse sebaka sa heno pele o jala.

Legumes di hloka bacteria tse loketseng le maemo a kgolo a loketseng hore di kgone ho fix nitrogen. Dimatlafatsi tse masalleng a tsona di a fumaneha ha thepa eo e ntse e bola.

Worm farms di ka fetola food scraps le bedding tse loketseng hore e be worm castings. Hlahloba bin ho e-na le ho lebella letsatsi le behilweng la kotulo.

Liquid that drains naturally from a worm bin e bitswa leachate. Ha o tshwane le worm-casting tea e lokisitsweng.

Leachate e ka ba le harmful organisms kapa substances. O se ke wa e sebedisa hodima edible plants kapa wa nahana hore ho e hlapolla ho etsa hore e bolokehe.

Tšimo ea Highveld e siiloeng e sa koaheloa ka mor’a kotulo ea maize e tobana le likotsi tse peli tse kholo.

Moea oa mariha o ka nka mobu o ommeng o ka holimo.

Sefefo sa pele se matla sa selemo se ka otla mobu o sa koaheloang ’me sa senya bokaholimo le sebopeho sa mobu. Ha metsi a phalla holim’a tšimo, a ka nka mobu o khoehileng.

Cover crops, mulch le organic matter di ka thusa ho tshwara mobu sebakeng sa wona le ho o thusa hore o dule o phela.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Protect exposed soil with suitable cover
keyPoints.sesothoDraft: Sireletsa mobu o pepesitsweng ka sekwahelo se loketseng

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Keep mulch away from trunks and stems
keyPoints.sesothoDraft: Boloka mulch hole le dithito le makala a dimela

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Choose cover crops for local water, weather and the following crop
keyPoints.sesothoDraft: Kgetha dijalo tse sireletsang mobu ho latela metsi a lehae, maemo a lehodimo le sejalo se latelang

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Worm-bin leachate is not automatically safe fertiliser; keep it off edible plants
keyPoints.sesothoDraft: Leachate ya worm bin ha ya lokela ho nkwa e le fertiliser e bolokehileng ka bohona; do not use it on edible plants.

question.sourceEnglish: A Highveld farmer harvests maize in April and leaves the field bare all winter. What are the two main risks?
question.sesothoDraft: Molemi wa Highveld o kotula poone (maize) ka Mmesa mme o siya tshimo e hlobotse mariha kaofela. Dikotsi tse pedi tse ka sehloohong ke dife?

options.sourceEnglish: Overheating in winter sun and waterlogging from rain
options.sesothoDraft: Ho tjhesa ho tlola tekanyo letsatsing la mariha le ho kopa metsi ho tswa puleng

options.sourceEnglish: Frost kills soil life and weeds take over early
options.sesothoDraft: Serame se bolaya bophelo ba mobu mme mefoka e nka sebaka pele ho nako

options.sourceEnglish: Wind erosion of dry topsoil and loss of soil structure from spring storm impact
options.sesothoDraft: Wind erosion ya topsoil e ommeng le tahlehelo ya soil structure ka lebaka la tshusumetso ya spring storm.

options.sourceEnglish: Soil pH drops and nitrogen builds up
options.sesothoDraft: PH ya mobu e a theoha mme naetrojene e a bokellana

rationale.sourceEnglish: Bare soil is exposed to winter wind, which can carry away dry topsoil. Raindrop impact can damage the surface; where water runs over the field, it can carry loosened soil away.
rationale.sesothoDraft: Mobu o sa kwahelwang o pepesetswa moya wa mariha, o ka nkang topsoil e ommeng wa tsamaya nayo. Tshusumetso ya marothodi a pula e ka senya bokahodimo; moo metsi a phallang hodima tshimo, a ka nka mobu o hlephileng a o tlosa.

question.sourceEnglish: What should you remember about liquid draining from a worm bin?
question.sesothoDraft: O lokela ho hopola eng ka mokedikedi o rothang ho tswa moqomong wa diboko?

options.sourceEnglish: It is always safe on salad leaves
options.sesothoDraft: O dula o bolokehile kamehla hodima mahlaku a salate

options.sourceEnglish: It can contain harmful organisms or substances; dilution is not a safety guarantee
options.sesothoDraft: O ka ba le ditshedi kapa dintho tse kotsi; ho o hlapolla hase tiisetso ya polokeho

options.sourceEnglish: It is identical to finished worm castings
options.sesothoDraft: O tshwana hantle le manyolo a phethilweng a diboko (worm castings)

options.sourceEnglish: A fixed dilution makes every liquid safe
options.sesothoDraft: Ho hlapolla ho itseng ho behilweng ho etsa hore mokedikedi o mong le o mong o bolokehe

rationale.sourceEnglish: Leachate is liquid that drains naturally from a worm bin. Its composition varies, so it must not be presented as a guaranteed safe feed for edible crops.
rationale.sesothoDraft: Leachate ke liquid that drains naturally from a worm bin. Composition ya yona e a fapana, kahoo ha ya lokela ho hlahiswa jwalo ka feed e bolokehileng ka tiisetso bakeng sa edible crops.

body.tshivendaDraft:
Mavu a na mifuda minzhi ya living organisms. Bacteria na fungi dzi thusa u kwashekanya organic matter na u cycle nutrients.

Dziṅwe fungi dzi thusa midzi u dzhia nutrients. Worm channels dzi nga thusa uri maḓi na muya zwi dzhene mavuni.

Sedzani midzi, tshivhumbeo tsha mavu na u tshimbila ha maḓi, ni dovhe ni sedze zwithu zwi tshilaho zwine zwa vhonala mavuni.

Vheani soil na water kha clear jar, ni engedze little suitable dispersing detergent. Ni vale jar, ni i dzinginye, ni i sie i sa tshintshwi.

Sand i settles pele. Silt i settles nga murahu, ngeno clay i tshi nga sala i suspended much longer.

Hezwi ndi rough learning exercise. Clumps na clay i sa athu settled zwi nga ni xedza; shumisani soil laboratory musi accurate texture i tshi ṱoḓea.

Vhambedzani zwipiḓa zwe zwa dzula fhasi, ni dovhe ni fare mavu tsimuni.

Ṅwalani zwe na zwi vhona na zwine zwa kha ḓi sa vha khagala. Ni songo dzhia phetho ya u sheledza kana u lafha mavu nga u sedza jar nthihi fhedzi.

Compaction, poor drainage na loss ya organic matter zwi nga limit midzi na soil life.

Pale colour kana few worms a zwi prove uri chemicals dzo vhulaha mavu. U shuma ha worms na hone hu a shanduka u ya nga moisture na season.

Sedzani patterns tsimuni. Sedzani management history, drainage na u aluwa ha plants ni sa athu khetha remedy.

title.tshivendaDraft: U Ita na U Shumisa Khomposo (Compost)

body.sourceEnglish:
Compost is organic matter broken down under managed conditions.

Finished compost can improve soil structure and contribute nutrients.

Time to readiness varies with materials, moisture, air and temperature. A province name or a fixed number of weeks is not a readiness test.

Mix dry browns with fresh greens. Avoid thick, wet layers that keep air out.

If the heap becomes slimy or smells strongly of ammonia, add dry browns and turn it.

Check moisture and air as the heap changes; one recipe does not suit every mix of materials.

A hot centre does not prove that every part of a heap has been treated. Time, temperature and management all matter.

Keep meat, dairy, diseased plants, pet waste and contaminated materials out of this simple household system.

Do not assume home composting destroys every weed seed or disease organism. Use a recognised process where sanitation is required.

Keep wattle seed pods out of the compost heap. An ordinary heap may not make every seed non-viable.

Use only clean, untreated materials. Bark breaks down slowly; its name alone is not proof that it is free of contamination.

Check the heap and turn when it needs more air or mixing. Keep it moist rather than waterlogged.
body.tshivendaDraft:
Compost ndi organic matter yo broken down nga fhasi ha managed conditions.

Compost yo fhelelaho i nga khwinifhadza tshivhumbeo tsha mavu, na u contribute nutrients.

Tshifhinga tsha u luga ha manyoro tshi a fhambana u ya nga zwishumiswa (materials), vhunyunyu, muya na thempheretsha (temperature). Dzina ḽa vundu kana mbalo yo vhewaho ya vhege a si tsedzuluso ya u luga ha manyoro.

Tanganyani dry browns na fresh greens. Avoid thick, wet layers that keep air out.

Arali thulwi ya manyoro ya vha slimy kana ya nukha ammonia nga maanḓa, shelani dry browns nahone ni i rembuluse.

Sedzulusani vhunyunyu na muya musi thulwi i tshi khou shanduka; recipe nthihi a i lulameli mutanganyo muṅwe na muṅwe wa materials.

Hot centre a i khwaṱhisedzi uri tshipida tshiṅwe na tshiṅwe tsha thulwi tsho treated. Time, temperature na management zwoṱhe zwi na ndeme.

Iledzani u dzhenisa nyama, dairy, zwimela zwi re na malwadze, pet waste na contaminated materials kha iyi simple household system.

Ni songo humbula uri home composting i fhedza weed seed iṅwe na iṅwe kana disease organism iṅwe na iṅwe. Shumisani recognised process hune sanitation ya ṱoḓea.

Iledzani u dzhenisa wattle seed pods kha thulwi ya manyoro. An ordinary heap may not make every seed non-viable.

Shumisani fhedzi clean, untreated materials. Bark breaks down slowly; dzina layo fhedzi a si proof ya uri a i na contamination.

Sedzulusani thulwi ni i rembuluse musi i tshi toda muya wo engedzeaho kana u tanganiswa. Keep it moist, hu si waterlogged.

title.sourceEnglish: Mulching and Cover Crops: Protecting and Building Soil
title.tshivendaDraft: Mulching and Cover Crops: U tsireledza mavu na Building Soil

body.sourceEnglish:
Cover bare soil with suitable clean mulch, such as straw, dry grass or wood chips.

Mulch can reduce evaporation, soften the impact of rain and suppress weeds.

Keep it clear of trunks and stems. Check moisture underneath and adjust the layer; more mulch is not always better.

Cover crops can protect ground between main crops. Choose for local weather, available water and the next planting.

The course examples include oats, lupins, sunn hemp and cowpea. Check local suitability before sowing.

Legumes need suitable bacteria and growing conditions to fix nitrogen. Nutrients in their residues become available as the material decomposes.

Worm farms can turn suitable food scraps and bedding into castings. Check the bin rather than expecting a fixed harvest date.

Liquid that drains naturally from a worm bin is called leachate. It is not the same as a prepared worm-casting tea.

Leachate can contain harmful organisms or substances. Do not use it on edible plants or assume that dilution makes it safe.

A Highveld field left bare after the maize harvest faces two main risks.

Winter wind can carry away dry topsoil.

The first heavy spring storm can strike bare ground and damage its surface and structure. If water runs over the field, it can carry loosened soil away.

Cover crops, mulch, and organic matter can help hold soil in place and help it stay alive.
body.tshivendaDraft:
Fukedzani mavu a songo fukwaho nga mulch yo kunaho, yo teaho, u fana na straw, hatsi ho omaho kana wood chips.

Mulch i nga fhungudza evaporation; i nga soften the impact of rain; i nga suppress weeds.

Keep it clear of trunks and stems. Sedzani moisture nga fhasi hayo ni lulamise layer; mulch nnzhi a i dzuli i tshi vha yavhuḓi.

Cover crops dzi nga tsireledza mavu vhukati ha main crops. Khethani u ya nga mutsho wa henefho, maḓi ane a vha hone na next planting.

Tsumbo dza course dzi katela oats, lupins, sunn hemp na cowpea. Sedzani arali dzi tshi fanela fhethu haṋu ni sa athu dzi zwala.

Legumes dzi ṱoḓa bacteria dzo teaho na growth conditions dzo teaho u fix nitrogen. Nutrients dzi re kha masalela adzo dzi a wanala musi material i tshi decompose.

Worm farms dzi nga shandula food scraps na bedding zwo teaho zwa vha castings. Sedzani bin, ni songo lavhelela fixed harvest date.

Liquid that drains naturally from a worm bin i vhidzwa leachate. A si tshithu tshithihi na prepared worm-casting tea.

Leachate i nga vha na harmful organisms kana substances. Do not use it on edible plants or assume that dilution makes it safe.

Field ya Highveld yo salaho i songo fukedzwa nga murahu ha harvest ya maize i sedzana na risks mbili khulwane.

Mhepo ya winter i nga hwala topsoil yo omaho ya i bvisa.

Storm ya u thoma khulwane ya spring i nga rwa mavu a songo fukedzwaho, ya tshinyadza surface na structure ya hone. Arali maḓi a tshi elela nṱha ha field, a nga hwala loosened soil a a bvisa.

Cover crops, mulch na organic matter zwi nga thusa u fara mavu fhethu hayo na u thusa uri a dzule a tshi khou tshila.

title.sourceEnglish: Understanding Your Soil: The Foundation of Everything
title.xitsongaDraft: Ku twisisa misava ya wena: Masungulo ya swilo hinkwawo

body.sourceEnglish:
Soil contains many kinds of living organisms. Bacteria and fungi help break down organic matter and cycle nutrients.

Some fungi help roots take up nutrients. Worm channels can help water and air enter soil.

Look at roots, soil structure and water movement as well as visible soil life.

Put soil and water in a clear jar, with a little suitable dispersing detergent. Close and shake it, then leave it undisturbed.

Sand settles first. Silt settles next, while clay can remain suspended much longer.

This is a rough learning exercise. Clumps and unsettled clay can mislead you; use a soil laboratory when accurate texture is needed.

A thick sand layer beneath cloudy water does not yet tell you the final proportions. Some fine particles may still be suspended.

Compare the settled layers and feel the soil in the field.

Record what you see and what remains uncertain. Do not prescribe watering or soil treatments from one jar alone.

Compaction, poor drainage and loss of organic matter can limit roots and soil life.

Pale colour or few worms do not prove that chemicals killed the soil. Worm activity also changes with moisture and season.

Look for patterns across the field. Check management history, drainage and plant growth before choosing a remedy.
body.xitsongaDraft:
Misava yi na tinxaka to tala ta swilo leswi hanyaka. Bacteria na fungi swi pfuna ku fayelela organic matter ni ku cycle nutrients.

Fungi tin'wana ti pfuna timitsu ku tswonga nutrients. Worm channels ti nga pfuna mati na moya ku nghena emhlabeni.

Languta timitsu, xivumbeko xa misava ni ndlela leyi mati ma fambaka ha yona, swin’we ni leswi hanyaka emisaveni leswi u swi vonaka.

Chela misava na mati eka clear jar, u chela nyana suitable dispersing detergent. Pfala jar u yi ninginika, kutani u yi tshika yi nga ninginiki.

Sand yi sungula ku tshamisa ehansi. Silt yi tshamisa endzhaku ka yona, kasi clay yi nga ha sala yi suspended much longer.

Lowu i rough learning exercise. Clumps na clay leyi nga si tshamaka ehansi swi nga ku hambukisa; tirhisa soil laboratory loko ku laveka accurate soil texture.

Thick sand layer ehansi ka cloudy water a yi si komba final proportions. Fine particles tin’wana ti nga ha va suspended.

Fananisa swiyenge leswi tshamaka ehansi, kutani u twa misava ensin'wini.

Tsala leswi u swi vonaka ni leswi nga si tiyiseka. U nga teki xiboho xa ku cheleta kumbe ku tirhisa ndlela yo lulamisa misava hi ku ya hi jar yin’we ntsena.

Compaction, poor drainage na ku lahleka ka organic matter can limit timitsu ni soil life.

Muhlovo lowu nga vonakaka wa pale kumbe few worms a swi tiyisisi leswaku chemicals ti dlayile misava. Worm activity na yona ya cinca hi ku ya hi moisture na season.

Languta patterns leti humelelaka ensin'wini hinkwaro. Kambela management history, drainage ni ku kula ka swimilani u nga si hlawula remedy.

title.sourceEnglish: Mulching and Cover Crops: Protecting and Building Soil
title.xitsongaDraft: Ku Tirhisa Mulch na Cover Crops: Ku Sirhelela Misava na Building Soil

body.sourceEnglish:
Cover bare soil with suitable clean mulch, such as straw, dry grass or wood chips.

Mulch can reduce evaporation, soften the impact of rain and suppress weeds.

Keep it clear of trunks and stems. Check moisture underneath and adjust the layer; more mulch is not always better.

Cover crops can protect ground between main crops. Choose for local weather, available water and the next planting.

The course examples include oats, lupins, sunn hemp and cowpea. Check local suitability before sowing.

Legumes need suitable bacteria and growing conditions to fix nitrogen. Nutrients in their residues become available as the material decomposes.

Worm farms can turn suitable food scraps and bedding into castings. Check the bin rather than expecting a fixed harvest date.

Liquid that drains naturally from a worm bin is called leachate. It is not the same as a prepared worm-casting tea.

Leachate can contain harmful organisms or substances. Do not use it on edible plants or assume that dilution makes it safe.

A Highveld field left bare after the maize harvest faces two main risks.

Winter wind can carry away dry topsoil.

The first heavy spring storm can strike bare ground and damage its surface and structure. If water runs over the field, it can carry loosened soil away.

Cover crops, mulch, and organic matter can help hold soil in place and help it stay alive.
body.xitsongaDraft:
Funengetani misava leyi nga hava cover hi mulch leyi basekile, leyi faneleke, yo fana na straw, byanyi byo oma kumbe wood chips.

Mulch yi nga hunguta evaporation; yi nga olovisa ku ba ka mpfula naswona yi nga suppress weeds.

Keep it clear of trunks and stems. Kambelani moisture ehansi ka yona, mi lulamisa layer; mulch yo tala a yi vuli leswaku swi ta antswa nkarhi wun'wana ni wun'wana.

Cover crops ti nga sirhelela misava leyi nga kona between main crops. Ti hlawuleni hi ku ya hi weather ya laha, mati lama kumekaka ni next planting.

Swikombiso swa course swi katsa oats, lupins, sunn hemp na cowpea. Kambelani loko swi fanele ndhawu ya kwalaho mi nga si swi byala.

Legumes ti lava bacteria leti faneleke ni suitable growing conditions leswaku ti fix nitrogen. Nutrients leti nga eka masalela ya tona ta kumeka loko material yi ri karhi yi bola.

Worm farms ti nga hundzuluxa food scraps ni bedding leswi faneleke swi va castings. Kambelani bin ematshan'weni yo langutela fixed harvest date.

Liquid that drains naturally from a worm bin yi vuriwa leachate. A yi fani na prepared worm-casting tea.

Leachate yi nga va na harmful organisms kumbe substances. Do not use it on edible plants or assume that dilution makes it safe.

Nsimu ya Highveld leyi tshikiweke yi nga funengetiwangi endzhaku ka ntshovelo wa maize yi langutana ni makhombo mambirhi lamakulu.

Mheho wa xixika wu nga susa misava ya le henhla leyi omeke.

Xidzedze xo sungula xo tika xa ximun’wana xi nga hlasela misava leyi nga funengetiwangi, xi onha vuandlalo ni xivumbeko xa yona. Loko mati ma khuluka ehenhla ka nsimu, ma nga teka misava leyi ntshunxekeke ma famba na yona.

Cover crops, mulch ni organic matter swi nga pfuna ku khoma misava endhawini ya yona ni ku yi pfuna leswaku yi ya mahlweni yi hanya.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Protect exposed soil with suitable cover
keyPoints.xitsongaDraft: Sirhelela misava leyi paluxiweke hi cover leyi faneleke.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Keep mulch away from trunks and stems
keyPoints.xitsongaDraft: Hlayisa mulch ekule na trunks na stems.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Choose cover crops for local water, weather and the following crop
keyPoints.xitsongaDraft: Hlawula cover crops hi ku ya hi mati ya laha, weather ni crop leyi landzelaka.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Worm-bin leachate is not automatically safe fertiliser; keep it off edible plants
keyPoints.xitsongaDraft: Worm-bin leachate is not automatically safe fertiliser; yi hlayise ekule na edible plants.

question.sourceEnglish: A Highveld farmer harvests maize in April and leaves the field bare all winter. What are the two main risks?
question.xitsongaDraft: Murimi wa Highveld u tshovela maize hi April kutani a siya field yi nga funengetiwangi all winter. Hi wahi makhombo mambirhi lamakulu?

options.sourceEnglish: Overheating in winter sun and waterlogging from rain
options.xitsongaDraft: Ku hisa ngopfu ehansi ka dyambu ra winter ni waterlogging from rain

options.sourceEnglish: Frost kills soil life and weeds take over early
options.xitsongaDraft: Frost kills soil life naswona weeds take over early

options.sourceEnglish: Wind erosion of dry topsoil and loss of soil structure from spring storm impact
options.xitsongaDraft: Wind erosion ya dry topsoil ni ku lahlekeriwa hi soil structure hi ku ba ka spring storm

options.sourceEnglish: Soil pH drops and nitrogen builds up
options.xitsongaDraft: Soil pH ya hunguteka naswona nitrogen ya hlengeletana

rationale.sourceEnglish: Bare soil is exposed to winter wind, which can carry away dry topsoil. Raindrop impact can damage the surface; where water runs over the field, it can carry loosened soil away.
rationale.xitsongaDraft: Misava leyi nga funengetiwangi yi va erivaleni eka mheho wa winter, lowu nga susaka dry topsoil. Ku ba ka marhonsi ya mpfula ku nga onha surface; laha mati ma khulukaka ehenhla ka field, ma nga teka misava leyi ntshunxekeke ma yi susa.

question.sourceEnglish: What should you remember about liquid draining from a worm bin?
question.xitsongaDraft: U fanele ku tsundzuka yini hi liquid draining from a worm bin?

options.sourceEnglish: It is always safe on salad leaves
options.xitsongaDraft: Yi hlayisekile minkarhi hinkwayu eka salad leaves

options.sourceEnglish: It can contain harmful organisms or substances; dilution is not a safety guarantee
options.xitsongaDraft: Yi nga va na harmful organisms kumbe substances; dilution a hi safety guarantee

options.sourceEnglish: It is identical to finished worm castings
options.xitsongaDraft: Yi fana hi ku helela na finished worm castings

options.sourceEnglish: A fixed dilution makes every liquid safe
options.xitsongaDraft: Dilution yo karhi leyi vekiweke yi endla leswaku liquid yin'wana ni yin'wana yi hlayiseka

rationale.sourceEnglish: Leachate is liquid that drains naturally from a worm bin. Its composition varies, so it must not be presented as a guaranteed safe feed for edible crops.
rationale.xitsongaDraft: Leachate i liquid that drains naturally from a worm bin. Composition ya yona ya hambana, hikokwalaho a yi fanelanga ku kombisiwa yi ri feed leyi tiyisekisiweke leswaku yi hlayisekile eka edible crops.
